title: Query Plans, Indexes, and Transactions: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Query Plans, Indexes, and Transactions: Visual Guide

1. The Plan Tree | the same join-and-aggregate query as a good plan and a bad one, each operator tappable with its estimated and actual row counts | read a plan from the leaves upward and check estimated against actual rows first, because a bad row estimate is what causes the bad operator choice above it

2. Sargable Or Not | six WHERE predicates over a 100-million-row table, each showing how many rows the engine must examine and the rewrite where one exists | an index can only be seeked when the column sits bare in the comparison, so a function, cast or arithmetic on the column forces a full scan

3. Two Kinds Of Index | a B-tree on (tenant_id, created_at) beside an inverted index on body, with four queries sent to both | a B-tree stores ordered row keys and an inverted index stores terms mapped to postings, so LIKE with a leading wildcard is a grain problem rather than a tuning problem

4. Four Letters | five scenarios naming which ACID property is at stake, including one where every constraint passes and the outcome is still wrong | atomicity, isolation and durability each fail differently, consistency only means declared invariants, and transaction boundaries are a design decision

5. Two Shapes Of Work | a point lookup and a five-billion-row aggregate run against row-oriented and columnar storage, showing columns touched and bytes read | OLTP wants selective row-oriented access and OLAP wants columnar scans, and the two interfere when forced onto one engine
